questions.q: What does Python require to create a variable?
options: Just a name, an equals sign, and a value — no declaration keyword or upfront type
A type declaration before the variable name
A special keyword like 'var' or 'let'
Registration in a separate configuration file
questions.explain: Python infers the type from the value itself, with no separate declaration step.

options: A variable's type comes from its current value, rather than being locked to a declared type
A feature that makes all variables permanently type Any
A way to declare multiple types for one variable simultaneously
A Spark-specific feature unrelated to Python itself
questions.explain: This is why the same variable name could hold an int at one point and a string later, though doing so intentionally is rare.

questions.q: What does the type() function do?
options: Confirms what type Python actually decided a value is
Converts a value from one type to another
Deletes a variable
Declares a new variable's type in advance
questions.explain: type() is a diagnostic tool for checking what Python inferred, useful when something behaves unexpectedly.

questions.q: Why is None different from 0 or an empty string?
options: None means a value was never recorded at all, while 0 or '' are actual recorded values
None and 0 are exactly the same in Python
None only applies to string variables, not numbers
None is just Python's word for a negative number
questions.explain: Confusing 'no value' with 'a zero value' is a common, genuine data engineering bug.

questions.q: In the NYC Taxi data, which real column is a good example of a str, even though it looks numeric?
options: VendorID — stored as text in the raw file
fare_amount
trip_distance
passenger_count
questions.explain: VendorID is stored as text even though its values look like numbers, which is why checking a column's actual type matters.
